narrative.overview:
TaskDesk is a tidy desk that is always there and never asks for attention. It is a native Windows 11 app on WPF's built-in Fluent theme (`Application.ThemeMode`), so the window, the controls, the type ramp and every colour come from Windows itself and follow Light, Dark and high contrast without a line of TaskDesk code. The design's job is restraint: calm Fluent surfaces, one list the eye can scan in a glance, and colour that appears only where it carries meaning (a Task that is Overdue, a Due that is today, a List's own colour).

Its signature is soft and small, and it should be reused, not reinvented: pill chips for Due and Tags, count badges in the sidebar and the rail, a List-colour stripe on each row. These pieces are built on Fluent's own brushes and radii, so they read as part of Windows, but together they make a TaskDesk screen recognisable. Density is that of a desktop tool used all day at mid-size: 14 px body text, rows that fit one line, panels that appear on demand rather than crowding the list.

All colour goes through theme resources. The colour tokens in this file are the Fluent theme's Light and Dark values, recorded so tools can render them (8-digit values are CSS `#RRGGBBAA`; Fluent's XAML writes the same colours as `#AARRGGBB`); the app itself never hard-codes them (the only literal colours are the six List presets, which are user data).
keyCharacteristics: Native Fluent first: every control is Fluent's own, restyled only through styles `BasedOn` the Fluent style.
Meaning-only colour: Overdue, Today and List colour are the only hues beyond the system accent.
A soft signature: pill chips, count badges, the List stripe.
List first, details on demand: the detail pane opens when asked and stays closed when closed.
Every look works in Light, Dark and high contrast, with meaning carried by text as well as colour.

rules.name: The Meaning-Only Rule
rules.body: Colour beyond the neutrals and the system accent marks a fact: Overdue, today, caution, or which List a Task belongs to. Never use colour for decoration.

rules.name: The Theme-Resource Rule
rules.body: Every colour in the app is a `DynamicResource` to a Fluent key or one of the meaning-named brushes (`OverdueBrush`, `TodayBrush`, `ListStripeBrush`); the only literal colours are the List presets. A new meaning gets a new named brush in `FoundationResources`, not a hex value in XAML.

rules.name: The Words-Too Rule
rules.body: In high contrast every signal colour becomes the system text colour, so meaning must also be in text: "Overdue" sits in the Overdue header and the badge shows a count.

rules.name: The Ramp-Only Rule
rules.body: Text uses one of the app's ramp styles (`TitleText`, `SubtitleText`, `BodyStrongText`, `BodyText`, `CaptionText`, `SecondaryCaptionText`, `FieldLabel`), each `BasedOn` Fluent's. No ad-hoc font sizes or weights.

rules.name: The One-Line Row Rule
rules.body: Row text never wraps: titles and captions are single-line with a trailing ellipsis, and the full title is in a tooltip. Fluent's text styles wrap by default, so rows set `NoWrap` explicitly.

rules.name: The On-Demand Rule
rules.body: The list owns the window. The detail pane opens on a click, Enter, F2 or a notification; it stays closed when the user closes it, and arrow keys only move the selection.

rules.name: The Fluent-Lift Rule
rules.body: New work may add lift, but only Fluent's own elevation, and only where it helps a surface read as in front, for example a card that responds to hover. Never invent a shadow value.

dos: **Do** base every style on the Fluent style it replaces (`BasedOn="{StaticResource {x:Type X}}"`) and merge it in `App.xaml` after `ThemeMode` is set.
**Do** take colour from Fluent keys or the meaning-named brushes through `DynamicResource`, and add any new meaning to `FoundationResources`.
**Do** reuse the signature pieces (pill chips, badges, List stripe) before designing a new one.
**Do** give every control a visible label and an `AutomationProperties.Name`, and check it in Light, Dark and high contrast.
**Do** keep rows to one line, with the full title in a tooltip.
**Do** let Windows' animation setting switch motion off; the 400 ms completion hold drops to zero.
donts: **Don't** hard-code a colour in XAML; only the six List presets are literal.
**Don't** use spacing resources of type `Double` for `Margin` or `Padding`; write `Thickness` values.
**Don't** add a second typeface or sizes outside the Fluent ramp.
**Don't** invent shadow values; use Fluent's own elevation or none.
**Don't** put more than one accent button in a dialog, or make a destructive action the Enter default.
**Don't** reopen a pane, panel or overlay the user closed without an explicit request.
**Don't** follow web conventions where Windows has its own (window chrome, dialogs, file pickers, notifications).
